First, we write the integral as

$$
{\int }_{1}^{{e}^{2}}\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{3})\,\text{d}x={\int }_{1}^{{e}^{2}}\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{3})\cdot 1\cdot \text{d}x.
$$

 

We will solve this problem using integration by parts. We start by defining $u$ and ${v}^{′},$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}u=\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{3})\, & ⟹\,{u}^{′}=\frac{3}{x} \\ {v}^{′}=1\, & ⟹\,v=\int 1\cdot \,dx=x\end{aligned}
$$

Using the formula of integration by parts, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{1}^{{e}^{2}}\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{3})\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{1}^{{e}^{2}}u{v}^{′}\text{d}x \\  & =uv{|}_{1}^{{e}^{2}}-{\int }_{1}^{{e}^{2}}v{u}^{′}\text{d}x \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{3})\,(x){|}_{1}^{{e}^{2}}-{\int }_{1}^{{e}^{2}}x(\frac{3}{x})\,\text{d}x \\  & =[\operatorname{ln}⁡(({e}^{2})^{3})\,({e}^{2})-\operatorname{ln}⁡({1}^{3})\,(1)]-3{\int }_{1}^{{e}^{2}}\text{d}x \\  & ={e}^{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡({e}^{6})-3x{|}_{1}^{{e}^{2}} \\  & =6{e}^{2}-3({e}^{2}-1) \\  & =3({e}^{2}+1).\end{aligned}
$$
